lines (‖): They overheard two people they know settle a bribe, and do not know whom to tell. ‖ A regular customer has stopped coming. The reason they've been given doesn't make sense. ‖ Someone left an item in their care and hasn't returned. The item is valuable. The absence is now suspicious. ‖ Three different people have asked them the same unusual question. None of them knew each other. ‖ They found something hidden in a place it shouldn't be. They put it back. They haven't told anyone. ‖ A traveller passed through asking which nights their door is left unbarred, and was gone by morning. ‖ Something they were told had been burned has turned up for sale. ‖ They have seen the same unmarked cart pass their door three nights running, and have not wondered why. ‖ Their oldest friend has started paying for drinks with new silver and will not say where it came from. ‖ They've been offered money to not ask questions about something they hadn't even started asking about. ‖ A document they were asked to witness contained a clause they noticed at the time and said nothing about. ‖ Their predecessor left something behind (in a place where it shouldn't have been), and they haven't reported finding it. ‖ A neighbour has accused them of moving a fence, and the neighbour has witnesses who were not there. ‖ They lent their savings to a friend who has since left, and the friend's family says there was no loan. ‖ Their landlord has doubled the rent and will lower it only if they report on the family next door. ‖ A letter addressed to them was opened before it arrived, and the sender says it carried money. ‖ Their son has been seen at night with people who do not work, and comes home with coin. ‖ A customer paid them with a ring that someone else has reported stolen. ‖ They saw an accident that was no accident, and the person responsible knows they saw it. ‖ An inheritance they did not expect has arrived from a relative they never met, along with that relative's debts. ‖ Their spouse has been making payments to someone every month for years, and will not say who. ‖ Two neighbours have each asked them to stand witness in the same dispute, on opposite sides. ‖ They told a lie to protect a friend, and the friend is now repeating it to people who matter. ‖ A child they took in as a favour has family who want the child back, and want paying for the years. ‖ Their best customer owes them a year's takings and has started avoiding their street. ‖ Someone has been asking the neighbours what time they leave in the morning and when they come home. ‖ A tool they lent out came back broken, and the borrower insists it was broken when it left. ‖ They have been invited to the wedding of someone who once ruined their family, and refusing would be noticed. ‖ A purse they found and kept has a rightful owner, and that owner has started asking around. ‖ Their partner in a small venture has disappeared with the takings and left the debts in their name. ‖ A family they look after has stopped answering the door, and the shutters have stayed closed for a week. ‖ They agreed to hold a parcel for a traveller, and two different people have since come to collect it. ‖ An old letter of theirs, written in anger years ago, has been shown to the person it was about. ‖ Their apprentice has been talking to a rival, and came back with an offer to buy them out. ‖ Someone keeps paying off their small debts around the place before they can, and has left no name. ‖ A cousin has arrived to stay without warning, and spends every day watching one particular house. ‖ They found a name scratched into their door overnight, and it belongs to someone who died last winter. ‖ Their savings were hidden in a place only one other person knew, and the savings are gone. ‖ A neighbour's quarrel with them has gone before the people who settle disputes, and the hearing is next week. ‖ Someone close to them has been ill in a way nobody can name, and recovers whenever one particular visitor stays away.

A shipment they weren't expecting arrived and is now in their warehouse. They don't know who sent it or what to do. ‖ A business rival has offered them a partnership with terms so good it must be a trap. They can't find the trap. ‖ One of their most reliable suppliers has gone dark. The goods are still arriving. Someone else is sending them. ‖ They have evidence of price-fixing across the whole market. Publishing it helps their competition as much as their customers. ‖ A young trader has been undercutting them in ways that shouldn't be possible on their claimed capital. ‖ Someone is buying up their debts. Quietly. They don't know who, or why, or when they plan to call them in. ‖ A valuable cargo was reported lost at sea. The manifest has reappeared in a market two settlements away. ‖ Their master craftsman is talking to a rival. They haven't confronted them. They're not sure what they'd do. ‖ A contract they signed in difficult times has a clause they didn't fully read. Someone has read it. ‖ They have been slowly acquiring a controlling interest in a competitor through intermediaries. The competitor hasn't noticed yet. ‖ A supplier is providing goods of uncertain provenance. The price is too good to ask questions. People have started asking questions. ‖ A buyer has paid them in advance for a whole season of goods, far above the price, and will not say what the goods are for. ‖ Their bookkeeper has been taking a little from every sale for years, and the books balance only because the bookkeeper wrote them. ‖ A partner died owing them money, and the partner's heir says the debt was paid in a letter nobody can find. ‖ They sold a batch they knew was bad, and the customer it sickened is now asking who supplied it. ‖ A rival has hired away their two best hands in one week, on wages the rival cannot afford for long. ‖ They have promised the same order to two buyers, and both are due to collect on the same morning. ‖ A lender has bought the note on their shop and wants it settled by the end of the month. ‖ Their scales were tested and found heavy in their favour, and they swear someone changed them overnight. ‖ A family they put out of business has opened again under a new name, two doors down. ‖ Someone has been selling cheaper and worse goods under their mark, and customers are blaming them. ‖ They have quietly stopped paying a supplier who cannot afford to take them to law. ‖ A crate came to them by mistake, and the people who meant to receive it have started asking around for it. ‖ Their apprentice has been offered a partnership by a rival, on condition that the apprentice brings the recipes.

{…} now operates in ways {…} would not approve of. Neither discusses the divergence directly. ‖ {…} has one favour left to call in, and is saving it. {…} knows, and is watching for it. ‖ A third party has asked {…}, quietly, whether {…} can be trusted. {…} is about to call it in. ‖ {…} has begun to act like someone who considers the debt paid. {…} does not. ‖ Someone else has learned what favour {…} owes {…}, and now has a hold on {…} too. ‖ {…} has asked {…} for a vote against {…}'s own interests. {…} owes {…} a great deal, and neither has ever said so aloud. ‖ Years ago {…} did {…} a favour too large to repay, and {…} has been paying it back in small ways ever since. ‖ {…} owes {…} for an old kindness. {…} and {…} have each watched the other do good work. They argue, but each trusts the other's judgment in their own field. ‖ {…} and {…} disagree often and trust completely. Each has watched the other be right at cost, and neither forgets it. ‖ There is no arrangement between {…} and {…}, only a long record of kept words; in this settlement that makes them remarkable. ‖ {…} sends difficult cases to {…}, and {…} sends them back solved. A sealed letter arrived for them three weeks ago. They haven't opened it. They won't say why. ‖ They've been quietly buying up property in a district that hasn't been announced as a development site. Yet. ‖ One of their staff has started asking questions about records from seven years ago. They've been reassigned twice already. ‖ A merchant they spoke against has started praising them in public, and will not say why. ‖ Their most trusted advisor hasn't been seen in four days. The official story changes each time it's told. ‖ They know who committed a crime the guard is currently investigating. They're not telling the guard. ‖ Someone has been leaving anonymous notes in their office pointing to a colleague's corruption. The notes are accurate. ‖ They've been meeting privately with someone from outside the settlement whose identity they won't disclose. ‖ A routine appointment they made three weeks ago has been rescheduled four times. Each time they initiated the change. ‖ Someone who publicly supports them is being paid by someone who opposes them. They know this. ‖ They received a deposition in a civil case that, if acted on, would be correct, and would ruin someone they need. ‖ A clerk in their office has been copying letters at night, and the copies have turned up in a rival's hands. ‖ They signed an order last month on bad information, and the family it ruined has learned whose seal is on it. ‖ A petition they set aside has gathered names from half their street, and the people who signed it want an answer this week. ‖ Someone is collecting fees in their name, and the people paying think the receipts are honest. ‖ Their deputy has started answering questions meant for them, and people have begun going to the deputy first. ‖ An old ruling of theirs is being used to take a widow's house, and they cannot undo it without admitting the mistake. ‖ They promised the same post to two people, and both have already told their families. ‖ A ledger they swore was complete is missing the pages for one season, and an auditor is coming to read it. ‖ Their sister has been taking gifts from people who need their signature, and they found out from the person who paid most. ‖ They were seen leaving a house they had no business in, on the night its owner disappeared. ‖ A rule they wrote to stop one abuse has opened the door to another, and the people using it are their friends. ‖ Someone has forged their seal well enough to fool their own staff, and three orders went out under it before anyone noticed. ‖ They owe their post to a patron who has started asking for repayment in favours they cannot grant openly.

Someone else is working to pull {…} and {…} apart. ‖ The threat that brought {…} and {…} together is gone. Neither has said so aloud. ‖ {…} has taken a precaution against {…} that {…} was not meant to discover. {…} has discovered it. ‖ {…} has been dining with {…}'s rivals. {…} heard about it from a servant. ‖ {…} wants to bring a third member into the alliance. {…} thinks the newcomer would take {…}'s place. ‖ {…} voted against {…} on a small matter last week. {…} is waiting to see whether it was small. ‖ {…} and {…} both want the same office, and the alliance cannot survive one of them winning it. ‖ {…} has asked {…} to back a candidate {…} distrusts. {…} and {…} want the same thing and compete hard for it, but neither has let it turn into hatred. ‖ Only one of {…} and {…} can come out ahead, and both know it. They stay polite and give no ground. ‖ Every gain {…} makes, {…} answers within the season, and people here have learned to expect it. ‖ {…} and {…} bid for the same contracts and sit at the same tables. The settlement keeps score, and so do they. ‖ {…} wants {…}'s position, and {…} wants {…}'s reputation. They are civil in public and unforgiving in private. ‖ Every client {…} wins is one {…} lost, and the reverse. The balance between {…} and {…} has recently shifted. {…} has noticed; {…} has not, yet. ‖ A document {…} and {…} each believed only they possessed has turned up in someone else's hands. ‖ {…} has recently secured something that makes {…}'s hold obsolete. {…} and {…} are about to be on opposite sides of an important decision. ‖ {…} is being pressed to act against {…}, and has not mentioned it. ‖ {…} and {…} still respect each other, but what each of them wants is pulling apart, and both can see it. ‖ {…} has learned something about {…}'s family that {…} does not know. ‖ {…} has been offered {…}'s post by people who want {…} gone. ‖ {…} has made a mistake that {…} is bound to report. {…} has not reported it. ‖ The council has asked {…} and {…} to audit each other's accounts. One of their people is talking to the guard. They don't know which one yet. They're watching. ‖ A valuable item came through their network recently. Three different parties have asked about it quietly. ‖ Someone in the government takes their money and someone else's, and they do not know which side will be sold first. ‖ A job went wrong in a way that suggests information was leaked. They have three suspects. ‖ They're protecting someone from something worse. The someone doesn't know and wouldn't thank them. ‖ The same new face has turned up at three of their jobs, and they have put someone on to follow the newcomer. ‖ The guard captain has a file. They know because someone who works for the guard captain also works for them. ‖ Someone tried to rob them, and did it like a professional: no noise, the lock picked, nothing touched but the strongbox. ‖ Two of their people have started running jobs of their own, and are telling newer hands that the old boss is finished. ‖ A debt they called in was paid by someone they have never met, and that person now wants to meet. ‖ A load of theirs was taken on the road by people who knew the day, the route and the password. ‖ Someone has been using their name to frighten shopkeepers, and the shopkeepers have begun paying the wrong people. ‖ A child they pay to carry messages has stopped coming, and the last message never arrived. ‖ An honest official they have never managed to buy has started asking about one of their fronts by name. ‖ They are holding goods for someone who has stopped answering, and the goods are beginning to draw attention. ‖ A rival crew has offered peace, and the offer arrived on the same day one of their people went missing. ‖ Someone in their own crew has been skimming, and the sum matches exactly what a rival is now spending. ‖ A family they once ruined has a son who has just come of age, and he has started asking where they sleep.

Do one thing for {power} this season that the people who lead {power|it|them} cannot ignore. ‖ Be in the room the next time {power} must decide something that matters. ‖ Find a patron among those who lead {power}, and make {self} useful to them. ‖ Bring {power} a piece of news before anyone else does. ‖ Take on the work in {power} that no one else wants, and do it without complaint. ‖ Be asked for an opinion by those who lead {power}, once, this season.

Get {house} through the season without borrowing. ‖ Collect what is owed to {house} before the season is out. ‖ Cut the spending at {house} by a tenth this season, and keep the work going. ‖ Find {house} one more source of money. ‖ Pay every hand at {house} in full and on time this season. ‖ Keep the accounts of {house} balanced, and show them to anyone who asks.

Three guards have gone missing in the same district on night patrol. The report filed says they deserted. ‖ Weapons from the armoury have been disappearing in small quantities for months. The inventory matches, somehow. ‖ They received orders from above that contradict what they know to be right. They haven't acted on either yet. ‖ A prisoner in their custody knows something valuable. So does someone with reason to ensure they never speak. ‖ They've noticed the same group of faces at multiple locations where incidents occurred. No one else has. ‖ Someone is paying their soldiers more than their salary. The soldiers aren't saying who. ‖ A spy they turned is now being turned back, and feeding information in both directions. ‖ The ambush that killed two of their best people wasn't random. Someone knew the patrol route. ‖ A recruit they turned away has since joined a different outfit. The different outfit is now paying them to monitor this one. ‖ They are carrying out orders they believe are wrong. They have not yet decided at what point they stop carrying them out. ‖ A weapons cache they were responsible for is smaller than it should be. They haven't reported it yet. ‖ Two of the people under their command have been settling a private quarrel with drawn steel, and the rest are picking sides. ‖ An old comrade has turned up asking for a favour that could cost them their post if anyone learns of it. ‖ They signed for supplies that never arrived, and the merchant who sold them is already spending the money. ‖ Someone under their command has been selling duty rosters to people who want to know when the roads are empty. ‖ A report they wrote years ago blamed the wrong person for a death, and the right one has just come back. ‖ Their second has been meeting with the people they answer to, and orders have started arriving without passing through them. ‖ A deserter they let go quietly has been caught elsewhere and is telling everyone who let them walk. ‖ They have been ordered to clear a family off land the family has worked for generations, and the order is lawful. ‖ The pay chest came up short again this month, and the only other key belongs to someone they trust. ‖ A local family has been feeding the people under their command for free, and now expects a favour in return. ‖ One of their best people has asked to be released, and will not say what they are afraid of. ‖ Tracks they were told to ignore lead from the edge of the fields to a camp nobody has reported. ‖ They lost a wager to someone who now wants payment as a closed eye on one particular night.

Get the rights of {house} written down and sealed by those who govern, this season. ‖ Have those who govern confirm, in writing, who may give orders at {house}. ‖ Get {house} excused from one tax or levy this season. ‖ Make sure no new rule from those who govern costs {house} anything this season. ‖ Win {house} first call on any help those who govern can give this season. ‖ Have the old rights of {house} read out and recognised before anyone challenges them.

Something happened between {…} and {…} years ago that neither has forgotten. They function professionally. A parishioner confessed something to them three months ago. The information is dangerous. They cannot act on it. ‖ The holy relic in their keeping is not what everyone believes it is. Only they know this. ‖ Someone has been leaving offerings at the shrine that shouldn't be possible. The site has been sealed. ‖ A novice has the gift. They know what that means for the novice. Compliance is expected. ‖ A healing they performed was successful in a way they cannot explain. It's happened twice now. ‖ Their predecessor left a sealed letter to be opened at their death; it never was, and it is still where it was left. ‖ A member of their congregation is systematically working against the faith. From inside it. ‖ They have been asked to perform a ceremony they have theological objections to. The person asking has leverage. ‖ A donation was made to the institution under conditions the donor didn't disclose publicly. The conditions are becoming relevant. ‖ They know which of the current leadership will be the next to fall from grace. They are waiting. ‖ A family has asked them to bury someone the faith forbids burying, and has offered a gift too large to refuse quietly. ‖ The offerings have doubled this season, and they cannot find out who is giving or why. ‖ A preacher from outside has been drawing their congregation away, and saying things about them that are partly true. ‖ They married a couple in secret at one family's request, and the other family has just found out. ‖ A child in their care claims to hear the god speak, and the child has been right three times. ‖ They have stopped believing, have told no one, and still lead the prayers every week. ‖ Someone has been reading the private letters kept in their care, and two of those letters were confessions.

Beat {other} at something this season, in front of people who matter. ‖ Find the weak spot in what {other} is doing, and press on it. ‖ Win over one of {other}'s friends. ‖ Keep {other} from getting the thing they want most this season. ‖ Learn what {other} has been saying about them, and to whom.
